body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「加了 L2 regularisation 後 validation loss 下降了。是否可以說模型現在較公平？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「可以，regularisation 減少 overfitting，所以它不會偏向任何人。」

## 兩個問題不能互相代答

Regularisation 是讓模型不要把訓練資料的偶然細節記得太死。L1、L2、dropout 或早停，會對複雜度、權重或訓練過程加限制，目標是令未見資料上的 generalisation 較好。它不會自動定義「公平」是甚麼，也不會告訴你哪種錯誤由誰承受。整體 loss 降低，可以同時發生在某個重要 error slice 變差的情況。

Fairness 先是一個決定和傷害問題：輸出只排隊、建議、分派資訊，還是影響一個人可否得到服務？哪些錯誤值得特別看？是否有合法、必要、最小化的資料可用來檢查差異？不能因為想畫一張 subgroup chart 就蒐集敏感資料。若沒有合理資料、明確目的和人手處理途徑，應先限制系統用途，而不是把公平變成一個漂亮指標。

## 字寫得工整，不等於考題公平

把一張考卷的答案寫得更工整，可以減少抄錯字；但不代表題目本身對每個人都同樣合理。Regularisation 像把字寫穩，公平檢查是在問題目、評分和後果有沒有對不同人造成不對稱的困難。

## 答題時要交代嘅判斷

把 generalisation 與 operational error analysis 分開。先以一個可解釋 baseline 和固定 evaluation 確認模型有沒有過度擬合；再為已定義、合理且可受治理的 case slice，檢查 false positive、false negative、拒答、延遲或 human override 的分布。差異不是自動等於歧視，平均一致也不是安全證明。你要說明該比較對哪個決定有用、資料限制是甚麼，以及遇到不確定結果時誰接手。

## 答案何時會太薄

不要把一個 fairness library、單一 parity number 或「我去掉了敏感欄位」當終點。先做小而安全的 baseline：以 synthetic case 建立整體錯誤表和少量已設計的情境 slice；所有高影響 case 一律人手覆核。若用途本身需要自動拒絕、處分或排序真實個人，作品集範例不應假裝已找到風險可接受的解法。

## 技術證據

展示版本化訓練設定、regularisation choice、training/validation curve、固定 eval set、error taxonomy 和 slice report。每一個 slice 要有定義、樣本數、未知值處理和不應解讀為人口統計結論的註記。加入 unit test，確認缺失或不允許的欄位不能悄悄進 feature pipeline；保留 human override 和 abstain case 的 trace。

## 交付、業務與風險證據

`risk-boundary.md` 要寫清楚系統只支援何種低風險草稿或排序、誰可以覆核、何時停止、如何接受申訴或修正，以及哪些資料不蒐集。不要把 synthetic subgroup 結果寫成對真實群體的公平保證，也不要將較低 loss 說成已減少傷害。用一份 decision record 留下用途、非目標、資料最小化和人手 owner，才是能被追問的交付證據。

## 延伸閱讀

[由 offline evaluation 走到獲授權 pilot](/zh-HK/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot)、[安全、治理、私隱與 incident response](/zh-HK/articles/safety-governance-privacy-and-incident-response) 和 [model score 怎樣連回 workflow decision](/zh-HK/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。例子使用虛構 task 和 synthetic cases，不涉及真實群體、真實個人資料、任何機構政策或現實世界公平結果。

body.zh-Hans:
> 面试官问：“加了 L2 regularisation 后 validation loss 下降了。是否可以说模型现在更公平？”
>
> 答对一半的答案：“可以，regularisation 减少 overfitting，所以不会偏向任何人。”

## 两个问题不能互相代答

Regularisation 是让模型不要把训练数据的偶然细节记得太死。L1、L2、dropout 或早停，会对复杂度、权重或训练过程加限制，目标是让未见数据上的 generalisation 更好。它不会自动定义“公平”是什么，也不会告诉你哪种错误由谁承受。整体 loss 降低，也可能同时发生在某个重要 error slice 变差的情况。

Fairness 首先是决策与伤害问题：输出只排队、建议、分派信息，还是影响一个人能否得到服务？哪些错误值得特别看？是否有合法、必要、最小化的数据可用来检查差异？不能因为想画 subgroup chart 就收集敏感数据。若没有合理数据、明确目的和人工处理途径，应先限制系统用途，而不是把公平变成漂亮指标。

## 字写得工整，不等于考题公平

把一张考卷答案写得更工整，可以减少抄错字；但不代表题目本身对每个人都一样合理。Regularisation 像把字写稳，公平检查是在问题目、评分与后果是否对不同人造成不对称困难。

## 面试真正想听到的判断

把 generalisation 与 operational error analysis 分开。先用可解释 baseline 和固定 evaluation 确认模型有没有过度拟合；再为已定义、合理且可治理的 case slice，检查 false positive、false negative、拒答、延迟或 human override 的分布。差异不是自动等于歧视，平均一致也不是安全证明。你要说明比较对哪个决策有用、数据限制是什么，以及遇到不确定结果谁接手。

## 答案什么时候太薄

不要把一个 fairness library、单一 parity number 或“我去掉敏感字段”当终点。先做小而安全的 baseline：用 synthetic case 建立整体错误表和少量设计好的情境 slice；所有高影响 case 一律人工复核。若用途本身需要自动拒绝、处分或排序真实个人，作品集示例不该假装已找到风险可接受的解法。

## 技术证据

展示版本化训练设置、regularisation choice、training/validation curve、固定 eval set、error taxonomy 和 slice report。每个 slice 要有定义、样本数、未知值处理和不应解读为人口统计结论的注记。加入 unit test，确认缺失或不允许的字段不能偷偷进 feature pipeline；保留 human override 和 abstain case 的 trace。

## 交付、业务与风险证据

`risk-boundary.md` 要写清楚系统只支持哪种低风险草稿或排序、谁能复核、何时停止、如何接受申诉或修正，以及哪些数据不收集。不要把 synthetic subgroup 结果写成对真实群体的公平保证，也不要把较低 loss 说成已经减少伤害。用 decision record 留下用途、非目标、数据最小化和人工 owner，才是可被追问的交付证据。

## 延伸阅读

[从 offline evaluation 走到获授权 pilot](/zh-Hans/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot)、[安全、治理、隐私与 incident response](/zh-Hans/articles/safety-governance-privacy-and-incident-response) 和 [model score 怎么连回 workflow decision](/zh-Hans/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)。

## 范围说明

这是 AI.DOG 的单题练习。例子使用虚构 task 和 synthetic cases，不涉及真实群体、真实个人数据、任何机构政策或现实世界公平结果。
body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “After adding L2 regularisation, validation loss fell. Can you now say the model is fairer?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Yes. Regularisation reduces overfitting, so it will not favour anyone.”

## Two questions cannot answer each other

Regularisation helps a model avoid memorising accidental details of training data. L1, L2, dropout, and early stopping constrain complexity, weights, or the training path to improve generalisation on unseen data. They do not define what fairness means, and they do not identify who bears which error. Overall loss can fall while an important error slice worsens.

Fairness begins as a question about a decision and potential harm. Does the output only order a queue, suggest information, or affect whether someone receives a service? Which mistakes need special attention? Is there lawful, necessary, minimised data for checking a difference? You do not collect sensitive information merely to draw a subgroup chart. If there is no sound data basis, purpose, and human handling route, restrict the system's use before turning fairness into a flattering metric.

## Neater writing does not make an exam fair

Writing the answers on an exam paper more neatly can reduce copying mistakes. It does not make the questions equally reasonable for everyone. Regularisation is like writing more steadily. A fairness check asks whether the question, marking, and consequences create unequal difficulty for different people.

## The judgement an interviewer is listening for

Keep generalisation and operational error analysis separate. First use an interpretable baseline and fixed evaluation to check overfitting. Then, for defined, justified, governable case slices, inspect false positives, false negatives, abstentions, delays, or human overrides. A difference is not automatically discrimination, and average similarity is not proof of safety. Explain which decision the comparison informs, what the data cannot show, and who takes over for uncertainty.

## Where an answer goes thin

A fairness library, one parity number, or “I removed a sensitive column” is not an ending. Start with a safe baseline: synthetic cases, an overall error table, and a few intentionally designed scenario slices; route every high-impact case to human review. If the intended use automatically denies, penalises, or ranks real people, a portfolio example should not pretend it found an acceptable risk solution.

## Technical evidence

Show versioned training settings, the regularisation choice, training and validation curves, a fixed evaluation set, error taxonomy, and a slice report. Every slice needs a definition, sample count, treatment of unknown values, and a note that it cannot be read as a population claim. Add tests that block missing or disallowed fields from silently reaching the feature pipeline, and retain traces for human overrides and abstained cases.

## Delivery, business, and risk evidence

`risk-boundary.md` should state the low-risk drafting or ranking use only, who can review it, when it stops, how corrections are received, and which data is not collected. Do not present synthetic subgroup results as a fairness guarantee for real groups or lower loss as evidence of reduced harm. A decision record that names purpose, non-goals, data minimisation, and a human owner is the delivery evidence that can survive follow-up.

## Further reading

[Move from offline evaluation to an authorised pilot](/en/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot), [safety, governance, privacy, and incident response](/en/articles/safety-governance-privacy-and-incident-response), and [connect a model score to a workflow decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. It uses fictional tasks and synthetic cases only. It involves no real groups, personal data, organisation policy, or real-world fairness outcome.
